Acme

AK-mee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Acme is the highest or most perfect point of something, especially a quality or achievement.

Critics called the sculpture the acme of the artist's decades-long career, a work she never surpassed.

Worked Example

The tailor's hand-stitched suits were considered the acme of craftsmanship, each one taking over two hundred hours to complete.

Acme usually describes an example so perfect that it represents the very best possible version of a quality -- like the acme of patience, or the acme of bad taste.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

peak: A peak is the top of a rise -- a career peak, a fever's peak, peak traffic. It marks the moment or level at which something crested, and often a fall follows. The acme is not a moment in a story: it is the single most perfect example of a quality or craft.

height: Height, in this sense, is the most intense stretch of something ongoing -- the height of the storm, the height of the tourist season. It measures intensity in time. The acme is a benchmark instead: the most perfect instance of a craft ever produced, whenever it happened.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

nadir: the lowest point in someone's fortunes

depths: the lowest or most extreme negative point of something

Where it sits · how close to the very top — high-quality → acme → perfection

high-quality vs. acme: High-quality is a weaker claim than acme: it just means very good, while the acme goes further, naming the single highest, most perfect point something can reach.

perfection vs. acme: Perfection goes even further than acme, meaning absolute, flawless completeness, with literally nothing that could be improved.

Build the Word

The pieces

origin — akme

origin — akme: the highest point, peak (Greek akme, 'point, peak')

Put it together

Put it together: Acme comes directly from Greek akme, meaning 'the highest point' or 'peak' -- the same idea of a sharp, singular high point that the word still carries today.

Use the root in a new word: Acme Corporation

Use the root in a new word: Acme Corporation: Cartoons like Looney Tunes use 'Acme Corporation' as a joke -- the name literally means 'the best,' which makes it funny when Acme's gadgets always malfunction.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Acme is often used for the perfect, ultimate example of a quality -- sometimes seriously (the acme of skill), and sometimes ironically, to poke fun at how extreme something is (the acme of laziness).
